vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: At fa242f5e10511cb2400396ebb56964becef12799, Downloader._download_package writes bytes returned by urllib2.urlopen(info.url) to the package path and immediately calls unzip(filepath, zipdir) without comparing the received archive to the package-index checksum. The same first-write uses md5_hexdigest(filepath) only in _pkg_status(), which is the pre-download installed/stale decision. The same gap remains in tags 3.9.2, 3.9.3, 3.9.4, and v3.10.0-rc1; the latter uses a temporary path but still os.replace()s and extracts it without a post-download hash. This reproduces CWE-494 under a tampered response or malicious mirror.

atomic_bic.evidence: git log -L and reverse path history converge on fa242f5e10511cb2400396ebb56964becef12799 (2008-08-30, Edward Loper) as the first public write of both the download-then-extract path and the checksum-only status path. The commit adds nltk/downloader.py as a new file; subsequent URL compatibility, formatting, unzip, MD5-to-SHA-256, and status-check changes carry the original omission rather than introduce it.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: The BIC has the single, locally present parent 0465a4daad21fbab03956599f0f109aef1bb4f3d. git cat-file/tree inspection shows nltk/downloader.py and any download-named path are absent from that parent tree, while the BIC adds nltk/downloader.py, so the vulnerable implementation is absent immediately before the BIC.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: The BIC is a one-parent git-svn revision (svn/trunk@6522), not a move, revert, merge, or reconstructable squash. The closure 7a5740af89feeb739193db766e11e85dfe78339c is GitHub's one-parent squash of PR #3625. GitHub's PR API exposes five source members: 56a044599b6cfaa3026f57e3a86c7a328e49e746 adds size/SHA-256 verification before os.replace(), 16cad11a02251228c5e85ec5eccab4a2af817930 is formatting, 490799e00abd837a7e377027ff54a09cdd8c34b4 adds legacy MD5 verification, ebc046f88dc0c7472344e7cc7c14fbdeab79d9cc adds tests, and 52eb614a72efb9729e0fd32b62fed7ce9acdd505 merges upstream. Those member objects are not present in the frozen default-history clone, but the API patches independently decompose the squash.

affected_and_fixed_release_membership.evidence: The BIC is an ancestor of 3.9.2, 3.9.3, 3.9.4, v3.10.0-rc1, v3.10.0-rc2, and v3.10.0. Direct tag-file inspection finds no pre-extraction integrity check through v3.10.0-rc1. The fix is not an ancestor of 3.9.2, 3.9.3, 3.9.4, or v3.10.0-rc1, and is an ancestor of v3.10.0-rc2 and v3.10.0; both fixed tags resolve to bd49f9011d7dc8c6a36b3c4ae71f04060c9b3fb9. CVE.org and the vendor GHSA claim 3.9.3 unaffected/patched, but immutable tag contents disprove that boundary; the primary record already states this correction.

direct_fix_or_verified_unpatched_state.evidence: The parent 4085d53c7793d3d6622f2bf02272faf54d4c3975 still downloads to tmp_filepath, calls os.replace(tmp_filepath, filepath), and then _unzip_iter() without checking size or checksum. Its child 7a5740af89feeb739193db766e11e85dfe78339c inserts size plus SHA-256/legacy-MD5 checks on tmp_filepath before os.replace() and extraction, deleting and rejecting mismatches. git -S identifies this as the first default-history write of sha256_hexdigest(tmp_filepath), so it directly reverses the reviewed integrity gap.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: The BIC commit object alone names Edward Loper <edloper@ldc.upenn.edu> as both author and committer, dates to 2008-08-30, and contains no trailers or AI/bot markers (no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Copilot, Cursor, or bot identity). Fix/PR metadata was not used for BIC attribution. This supports NOT_AI.

findings: The primary mechanism, BIC, parent, direct-fix, release-membership, and BIC-only AI conclusions independently reproduce from the frozen clone.

The external advisory's >=3.9.3 patched boundary conflicts with repository tag contents; the primary record already detects and correctly replaces it with v3.10.0-rc2/v3.10.0 as the first fixed release tags.
PR #3625 is a squash, but its API-visible members confirm that the integrity fix is substantive rather than an unrelated aggregate effect.
